autonomous

aw-TAHN-uh-muss — stress the TON; think 'on its OWN-omous,' running on its own. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Autonomous is governing or operating independently, without outside control.

The island region became autonomous, making its own laws without approval from the mainland.

Example

The chess club writes its own budget, elects its own officers, and plans its own tournaments. It answers to no school committee and needs no adviser's signature. Every decision comes from the members themselves.

A group that runs itself without outside control is autonomous. Unlike 'free,' which just means unrestricted, autonomous emphasizes actively governing yourself and making your own rules.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

independent: Independent means not controlled or supported by others — a person, a shop, or a nation can be independent. Autonomous is more active: an autonomous group actually governs itself, writing its own rules and running its own affairs, rather than merely standing free of outside control.

self-governing: Self-governing means making and enforcing your own rules, so it fits councils, regions, and clubs. Autonomous is broader: anything that operates without outside control can be autonomous, including machines — an autonomous drone flies itself, though nobody would say the drone is self-governing.

self-sufficient: Self-sufficient means needing no outside help to function — you supply your own food, money, or materials. Autonomous is about control rather than supplies: an autonomous region makes its own decisions yet may still import everything it eats. One is about needs, the other about who is in charge.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

dependent: relying on someone or something else

subordinate: placed under another's authority

Where it sits · how fully it rules itself — free → autonomous → sovereign

free vs. autonomous: Free simply means unrestricted, which is weaker than autonomous — an autonomous group doesn't just lack restrictions, it actively governs itself.

sovereign vs. autonomous: Sovereign is stronger than autonomous: a sovereign nation holds complete, supreme authority, while an autonomous region governs itself but may still belong to a larger country.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — auto-

prefix — auto-: self (Greek)

root — nom-

root — nom-: law (Greek)

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: having the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Greek auto- (self) plus nomos (law) literally means 'having its own laws.' Something autonomous makes its own rules instead of following someone else's.

Use the root in a new word: astronomy

Use the root in a new word: astronomy: Astronomy is literally 'the law of the stars,' the study of the rules the night sky obeys.
